title: Ops & Eval: A/B compare and regression alerts demo - Nimbus Retail
summary: Redwood AE+SE walkthrough of the Eval/Quality Monitoring features (prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons) for Nimbus Retail's search-rewrite and personalization pipelines. Discussed integration approach, sample evals, alert thresholds, and pilot next steps. Customer raised questions about data residency, SSO and how A/B traffic split works with Dedicated instances.
next_steps: Jordan to share demo recording and slide deck (link)
Priya to export a starter prompt-set and example eval spreadsheet for Nimbus data
Schedule 2-week pilot kickoff with Nimbus eng team (proposed: 2025-09-23)
Nimbus to provide sample logs + 3 canonical prompts by 2025-09-18
action_items: Priya Nair | Upload starter prompt-set (CSV) and sample eval template | 2025-09-15
Alex Moreno | Send 3 example queries and redaction rules | 2025-09-18
Maya Li | Confirm pilot success criteria (latency, p95, accuracy delta) | 2025-09-16
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Um, quick intro — I'm Jordan Kim, AE for Redwood Inference. With me is Priya, our SE, and Samir who helps with integrations.
[00:06] Alex (Nimbus - Eng): Hey Jordan, thanks. Alex here, Maya, Ravi on the call. We're excited, we've been reading your docs on evals and alerts.
[00:13] Priya (Redwood SE): Great — today we'll walk through the Eval/Quality monitoring flows: building prompt-sets, how regression alerts fire, and the A/B compare experience in the console and via the API. We'll use a Nimbus demo dataset for search-rewrite examples.
[00:30] Maya (Nimbus - PM): Quick note: our legal team asked about data retention and residency, we are US-only, and any logs used in evals must be redact-first.
[00:37] Jordan: Good callout. We have options — can do redact in your pipeline, and for Dedicated/Private you can fully control retention and KMS. Priya will show the masking flow.
[00:45] Priya: Alright, jumping into the console — I'm sharing screen. Forgive the little typo in the deck, the product name rendered as "Reedwood Optimize" on slide 3, ha.
[00:58] [screen share noise]
[01:05] Priya: Here is the Eval tab. First step is building a prompt-set. You can upload CSVs, or link a live dataset. For Nimbus we'll demo a small CSV of 500 queries; we have columns: query_text, expected_rewrite, user_segment.
[01:22] Alex: Nice. How do you handle multiple references per input? In our system we sometimes have 2-3 correct rewrites depending on user segment.
[01:30] Priya: Good question — prompt-sets support multiple references per row; we store them as a list in the eval backend. The scoring supports pairwise and set-based metrics. For A/B we compute per-sample wins and ties.
[01:45] Samir (Redwood SE): Also the API accepts an array of expected outputs when you call the batch eval endpoint; we map that into the aggregate metrics.
[01:55] Maya: And the regression alerting — is it based on absolute thresholds or change-from-baseline?
[02:02] Priya: Both. You can configure absolute thresholds (e.g., accuracy below 90%) or delta-based alerts (drop > 3% from baseline). Baseline is either a rolling baseline or a pinned snapshot.
[02:14] Ravi (SRE): For production, noise is the issue. What about alert noise — can we set suppression windows and severity routing?
[02:20] Priya: Yes. You can set a suppression window, min sample counts, and route alerts to Slack, PagerDuty, or an internal webhook. We also support anomaly detection instead of simple deltas.
[02:32] Alex: How does this tie into A/B experiments on Dedicated instances? If we have two model variants on Dedicated pools, can A/B compare take into account different hardware latency?
[02:43] Samir: The A/B compare is model-variant aware. In the console we'll show per-variant token costs and p95 latency alongside quality metrics. You can filter comparisons by hardware tag or pool.
[02:56] Jordan: Let me show the A/B compare UI — Priya, can you flip to the compare view?
[03:01] Priya: Yep. Here: you select two runs, or a run vs. a baseline snapshot. The UI surfaces pairwise comparison table: wins/losses, average score, and examples where the models diverge. We sample examples and you can click to view the full prompt + both outputs.
[03:20] Maya: That's helpful — our PMs want the example-level view to triage whether differences are meaningful or hallucinations.
[03:27] Priya: Exactly — we also surface an "explain" column that highlights token-level overlap and confidence proxies. Note: confidence is model-provided; for open models we synthesize soft-similarity heuristics if logit info isn't available.
[03:48] [crosstalk]
[03:52] Alex: If we run a continuous rollout, can we attach an eval set that runs nightly? We want nightly regression detection with human-in-the-loop review for critical flips.
[04:01] Priya: Yes. We have scheduled eval jobs. For critical sets you can mark a prompt-set as "guardian" which requires manual review before rollout if a threshold is crossed. Those get tagged and routed to the review queue.
[04:13] Maya: Does the guardian queue allow stakeholders beyond engineers, like legal? We need legal to sign off on some rewrites.
[04:18] Priya: You can add reviewers by SSO groups. We integrate with SAML/SCIM for group sync.
[04:24] Ravi: On SSO — we need SAML + SCIM, RBAC with least privilege. Also audit logs exported for 12 months.
[04:32] Jordan: For Private/Dedicated, audit log retention and SAML are supported — you'll manage keys via KMS. We can share SOC 2/ISO docs.
[04:41] Maya: Great. Can you show an example alert email or Slack notification?
[04:45] Priya: Sure, switching to an alert example. Here: Subject: "Eval alert: Search-rewrite accuracy decreased 4.6% vs baseline". Body includes top failing prompt examples and a link to the A/B compare run. The webhook payload includes metric deltas and sample IDs.
[05:02] Alex: The sample IDs — do they contain raw user data? We need PII removed.
[05:07] Priya: By default sample ids are hashed. For shared examples the console shows redacted content. If you bring your own private deployment we can keep everything internal.
[05:16] Alex: Ok. About the API — can we trigger an on-demand A/B compare programmatically? We want to call it from our CI when a model artifact is pushed.
[05:25] Samir: There's a compare API. You POST two run IDs, optional filter, and a compare config; the endpoint returns summary metrics and a small CSV of top diffs. It streams results for large sets.
[05:36] Maya: Streaming is good. Our sets can be 100k queries. How long to run an A/B compare for 100k?
[05:42] Priya: For a 100k compare against token-light prompts we typically finish in 20-40 minutes on hosted infrastructure; on Dedicated it depends on pool size and batching config. We'll provide quantized kernels and we have batching suggestions in the Optimize tab to speed it up.
[06:00] Alex: Any sample numbers on cost? Rough guidance for 100k prompt-run compare?
[06:05] Jordan: It varies a lot — but the Optimize tool will give you pre-run cost estimates. For a small-run compare with 100k short prompts expect low hundreds of dollars on hosted; Dedicated per-run cost is generally lower if you have reserved throughput. We'll send a sample cost spreadsheet.
[06:20] [10:00 — skip forward, demo continues]
[10:04] Priya: Now switching to live demo of an A/B compare results page. I'm opening a run: Run-A vs Run-B. See this table — sample 1 here shows Run-A produces a shorter rewrite that preserves brand phrasing, Run-B introduces a paraphrase that could break downstream normalization. We tag this as a potential regression.
[10:25] Alex: Can alert thresholds be different per prompt-set? Some mission-critical prompts need a tighter delta bound.
[10:31] Priya: Yes, alerting policies are per-prompt-set or global defaults. You can also set per-segment thresholds.
[10:38] Maya: For the examples you highlight — are those chosen deterministically? We want triage reproducibility.
[10:44] Samir: Deterministic sampling is an option; we also do stratified sampling to surface edge-segment failures. There's an option for reproducible seed.
[10:52] [15:12] Jordan: Quick qualification: what's Nimbus's timeline for a pilot?
[15:17] Maya: We're aiming to pilot before Q4; engineering availability in late September. We want to test with two prompt-sets: search-rewrite and personalization CTAs.
[15:27] Jordan: Perfect. We'll scope for two prompt-sets and a 2-week pilot. Priya will prepare starter CSVs and a sample CI hook.
[15:35] Alex: A couple security questions — do you store embedding vectors or logs long-term?
[15:40] Priya: Embeddings are optional; you choose to persist them or not. Logs can be configured to expire; in Private you control retention policy. For hosted we have retention defaults and enterprise options.
[15:50] Maya: On the evaluation metrics — what do you recommend for retail search? BLEU is not great, we want semantic similarity and business metrics like revenue-lift proxy.
[15:58] Samir: We typically run a mix: semantic metrics (BERTScore-like), BLEU for syntactic, and custom business metrics you provide (e.g., click-through rate increase simulated from logs). The console lets you surface a composite score.
[16:12] Alex: Regarding noise again — can we set a min sample size before an alert triggers? We don't want false positives on small slices.
[16:18] Priya: Yes, set min-samples and min-effect-size. Also we support bootstrap confidence intervals for deltas.
[16:27] [20:00 — Priya shows API snippet]
[20:04] Priya: This is an example POST to /v1/evals/compare with body: {"run_a": "r-123","run_b": "r-456","min_samples": 500}. Response contains field-level deltas and an attachments link. (note: transcript may mangle some braces)
[20:18] Alex: Great — we'll wire that into our CI after model packaging.
[20:22] Maya: A nit — onboarding docs we saw mention a csv schema with "expected_outputs" but not clear on escaping newlines.
[20:30] Priya: Good catch. We support JSONL for complex outputs; our starter CSV template handles escaping. I'll attach the template.
[20:38] Jordan: Ok, let's talk logistics — pricing for pilot, and Dedicated options if we scale.
[20:44] Alex: Pricing question: we have 3 teams that may run evals. How does multi-team access and quotas work?
[20:51] Jordan: The Console has org-level quotas; you can set per-team projects and quotas. Pilot pricing is usage-based with a small professional services setup for integration. If you go Dedicated we provide committed capacity tiers. We'll follow up with numbers.
[21:05] Maya: Anything about exports — we may want to pull raw diffs to our internal data lake for downstream reporting.
[21:11] Samir: Exports are available via the API; large CSVs are staged to S3-compatible URLs (or your private endpoint for Private deployment).
[21:20] [25:00 — example failure case review]
[25:06] Priya: Here are five top failing prompts: prompt_42 shows insertion of location-specific slang, which breaks our taxonomy; prompt_77 drops a brand tag; prompt_88 hallucinated unsupported promo terms. You can flag examples for manual review and create a remediation ticket in the review queue.
[25:28] Alex: If we flag an example, can the remediation flow automatically update the prompt-set or create a training ticket?
[25:35] Priya: We integrate with Jira and linear-like tools; flagging can create tickets. Automated updates to prompt-sets are a manual step, we avoid automatic repairs without human sign-off.
[25:46] Maya: Makes sense.
[25:50] [30:00 — audience questions]
[30:05] Claire (Procurement): For the pilot, what's the standard NDAs and terms? We have procurement redlines about data processing.
[30:12] Jordan: We'll provide the enterprise terms and an addendum for data processing; for pilot we can do a lighter MOU. Procurement will get the security pack.
[30:20] Claire: Do you have SOC2/ISO docs?
[30:23] Jordan: Yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary, plus pen-test reports on request.
[30:30] Alex: One more technical — if we run labeled human evaluations, can the console ingest human rater judgments and integrate into scoring?
[30:38] Priya: Absolutely. We ingest rater CSVs and you can map labels to scoring functions. You can weight human labels higher in composite scores.
[30:45] Maya: Ok that's useful.
[30:48] [40:00 — wrap up]
[40:02] Jordan: Quick recap: we'll send demo recording, starter prompt-set template, pricing sheet, and security docs. Pilot kickoff tentatively 2025-09-23. Action items are on the doc. Anything else?
[40:15] Alex: Could you also share a quick sample of the webhook payload for alerts? That helps our SRE.
[40:21] Priya: Yes, will include an example payload in the follow-up.
[40:25] Maya: Also include instructions for configuring the guardian queue.
[40:29] Jordan: Got it. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and create the pilot ticket.
[40:35] [end of recording]
